stem.en: Milk kept at 4 degrees lasts a week; at 30 degrees it turns in a day. Kabir says "so cold kills the milk's microbes". What do their enzymes do at 4 degrees?

text.en: They keep their folds and work slowly. Cold does not unfold anything; it only slows the collisions, from III.6. Warm the milk and the microbes' enzymes pick up where they left off.

feedback.en: Cold does not break a fold; the pulls that hold it get stronger, if anything. Only heat and acid unfold.
At 4 degrees nothing is frozen. The enzymes are slow, not stopped, which is why the milk still turns in a week.

text.en: They work faster in the cold.

feedback.en: Cuts per second fall steadily as you cool, on every enzyme in the lab.

explanation.en: Cold slows and heat kills. A fridge is a slowing; a boil is an unfolding. Only one of them is undone by warming back up.
